binders: A universally quantified exponent p : ENNReal.
An existentially quantified measure μ on the discrete measurable space Fin 2.
Existentially quantified functions f, g : Fin 2 → Real.
conclusions: The inequality eLpNorm (f + g) p μ ≤ eLpNorm f p μ + eLpNorm g p μ is false.
mathematical_definitions: Fin 2 is a two-point space equipped with the top, hence discrete, measurable structure.
The sum f + g is pointwise real addition.
eLpNorm h p μ is the extended-valued Lp seminorm of h with exponent p and measure μ.
The addition on the right-hand side is addition in ENNReal.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every extended nonnegative real exponent p strictly between 0 and 1, there are a probability measure μ on a two-point space and two real-valued functions f and g on that space such that the usual triangle inequality for their Lp seminorms fails: the Lp seminorm of f + g is not at most the sum of the separate Lp seminorms.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The strict assumptions exclude p = 0 and p = 1; because p < 1, they also exclude the top element of ENNReal.
The conclusion is existential and does not prescribe μ, f, or g beyond the stated probability and inequality-failure conditions.
No separate measurability hypotheses on f or g appear; on Fin 2 with the top measurable space, every real-valued function is measurable.
The target says Not (a ≤ b) literally. Interpreting this as a > b uses the order properties of ENNReal rather than additional syntax in the target.
The probability-measure conjunct prevents μ from being an arbitrary zero measure, but it does not explicitly require both points to have positive mass.
The claim is not vacuous: its hypotheses restrict p, while its conclusion demands concrete witnesses satisfying a genuine negated inequality.
